claims.claim_pattern: The British created the Khalsa / Sikh identity in the 19th century
claims.explanation: This erases the 1699 Khalsa initiation by Guru Gobind Singh Ji and earlier Sikh institutional history.
claims.correction: The Khalsa was initiated by Guru Gobind Singh Ji on Vaisakhi 1699 at Anandpur Sahib, long before British rule in Punjab.

claims.claim_pattern: Sikhs are just a Hindu sect and not a separate religion
claims.explanation: Sikh tradition has distinct scripture, initiation (Amrit), and eternal Guruship in Guru Granth Sahib.
claims.correction: Sikhism is a distinct panth with the ten Gurus and Guru Granth Sahib as eternal Guru.

claims.claim_pattern: Guru Nanak Dev Ji never existed / is a fictional character
claims.explanation: Denialist claims contradict extensive janamsakhi tradition, early Sikh sources, and historical scholarship.
claims.correction: Guru Nanak Dev Ji (1469–1539) is the founding Guru of Sikhism with a well-attested historical tradition.

claims.claim_pattern: There is no caste equality in Sikhism / Gurus supported caste hierarchy
claims.explanation: Core Sikh teaching and Rehat practice reject caste hierarchy; langar and sangat embody equality.
claims.correction: Sikh doctrine rejects caste discrimination; equality is foundational in Gurbani and Rehat Maryada.

claims.claim_pattern: The Five Ks were invented by the British colonial army
claims.explanation: The Five Kakaars are articles of Khalsa faith associated with Guru Gobind Singh Ji's discipline, not British invention.
claims.correction: Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachera, and Kirpan are Khalsa articles of faith from the Guru period.

claims.claim_pattern: Guru Gobind Singh Ji appointed a living human Guru after himself instead of Guru Granth Sahib
claims.explanation: Mainstream Sikh doctrine holds that eternal Guruship was conferred on Guru Granth Sahib.
claims.correction: Guru Gobind Singh Ji conferred Guruship on the Guru Granth Sahib as eternal Guru.

claims.claim_pattern: Sri Guru Granth Sahib has more than 1430 Angs / secret missing Angs prove conspiracy
claims.explanation: Standard printed Guru Granth Sahib has 1430 Angs; secret-volume conspiracy claims are a common fabrication pattern.
claims.correction: Verify any Ang citation against BaniDB within Angs 1–1430.

claims.claim_pattern: Women cannot take Amrit or participate as equals in Sikh practice according to Gurus
claims.explanation: Mainstream Sikh teaching affirms spiritual equality of women and men.
claims.correction: Sikh doctrine affirms equality; women participate in Amrit, seva, and sangat.

claims.claim_pattern: Gurbani promotes hatred against other communities
claims.explanation: Selective quoting often strips verses from their spiritual context about ego, tyranny, or devotion.
claims.correction: Read the full shabad and established translations; Gurbani centers Naam, justice, and universal dignity.

claims.claim_pattern: Langar is only for Sikhs / foreigners are not allowed
claims.explanation: Guru ka Langar is historically and doctrinally open without distinction of background.
claims.correction: Langar welcomes all; eating together without status distinction is a core Sikh institution.

claims.claim_pattern: Sikhs worship idols / statues of Gurus as deities
claims.explanation: Rehat centers devotion on Ik Onkar and Guru Granth Sahib, not idol worship.
claims.correction: Mainstream Sikh practice does not endorse idol worship; the Guru Granth Sahib is the eternal Guru.

claims.claim_pattern: Operation Blue Star proves Sikhism is inherently violent
claims.explanation: Collective guilt narratives about a modern political-military event are not evidence about Sikh doctrine.
claims.correction: Discuss 1984 with careful historical sourcing; do not collapse doctrine into propaganda slogans.

claims.claim_pattern: Guru Nanak said Sikhs should abandon Gurmukhi and only use another language
claims.explanation: Fabricated Guru quotes about abandoning Gurmukhi are not found in authentic scripture indexes.
claims.correction: Check any attributed quote via BaniDB/GurbaniNow before accepting it.

claims.claim_pattern: Amrit and Rehat rules against tobacco were invented recently for politics
claims.explanation: Bajjar kurehits including tobacco prohibition are part of established Amritdhari discipline.
claims.correction: Rehat Maryada documents personal discipline including prohibitions for Amritdhari Sikhs.

claims.claim_pattern: This viral shabad is from Ang 2000 of Guru Granth Sahib
claims.explanation: Ang 2000 does not exist in the standard 1430-Ang Guru Granth Sahib.
claims.correction: Valid Ang citations are between 1 and 1430; verify with BaniDB.

claims.claim_pattern: Sikh Gurus taught that caste names determine spiritual rank
claims.explanation: Opposite of Gurbani's egalitarian teaching.
claims.correction: Spiritual worth in Sikh teaching is not based on caste hierarchy.

claims.claim_pattern: Guru Arjan Dev Ji never compiled any scripture
claims.explanation: Denial of Adi Granth compilation contradicts established Sikh history.
claims.correction: Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.

claims.claim_pattern: Kirpan is proof that Sikhism mandates attacking civilians
claims.explanation: The kirpan is an article of faith tied to responsibility and defense of righteousness, not a license for aggression.
claims.correction: Kirpan is one of the Five Kakaars; conflating it with terrorism is a propaganda distortion.

claims.claim_pattern: Mul Mantar was changed by SGPC and original was different political slogan
claims.explanation: Conspiracy variants of Mul Mantar circulating online are fabricated.
claims.correction: Mul Mantar on Ang 1 is stable in standard Guru Granth Sahib; verify via BaniDB.

claims.claim_pattern: Sikhism forbids education and modern medicine according to Gurbani
claims.explanation: No such doctrinal ban exists; this is a fabricated restriction narrative.
claims.correction: Sikh history includes learning, seva, and institutions for community welfare; treat medical-ban claims as false.

claims.claim_pattern: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's martyrdom story is fake colonial propaganda
claims.explanation: Denial of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's martyrdom is a revisionist misinformation pattern.
claims.correction: Sikh tradition and historical sources affirm Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's martyrdom in defense of religious freedom.

claims.claim_pattern: Taking photos of Guru Granth Sahib parkash and editing fake Gurmukhi overlays is fine for memes
claims.explanation: Edited overlays often insert fabricated lines while using sacred imagery for credibility.
claims.correction: Always OCR/transcribe and verify overlays against BaniDB before trusting meme posts.

claims.claim_pattern: Sikhi teaches that rituals alone can guarantee spiritual liberation
aliases: Rituals alone guarantee mukti in Sikhism
Performing ceremonies is enough for salvation according to Gurbani
Sikhism says outer rituals grant liberation automatically
claims.explanation: Guru Nanak Dev Ji criticised empty ritualism. Mukti is not sold by ceremonies; Naam, Hukam, ethical living, and Guru's grace are central.
claims.correction: Sikhi does not teach that rituals alone guarantee liberation. Outer rites without Naam and transformation of the mind are not a sufficient path to mukti.

claims.claim_pattern: Bathing at a pilgrimage site or holy river automatically washes sins and grants mukti in Sikhism
aliases: A holy dip washes all sins according to Gurbani
claims.explanation: Gurbani turns tirath inward: cleansing ego from the mind. A river bath is not taught as an automatic ticket to liberation.
claims.correction: Pilgrimage bathing is not an automatic guarantee of mukti in Sikh teaching; inner transformation is what Gurbani emphasises.

claims.claim_pattern: Doing Nitnem or taking Amrit automatically guarantees heaven no matter how one lives
aliases: Paath is a magic charm for salvation
Amrit ceremony alone saves you regardless of conduct
claims.explanation: Nitnem and Amrit are discipline and commitment, not a charm that overrides hukam, naam, and ethical life.
claims.correction: Rehat practices are spiritual discipline, not a vending-machine guarantee of heaven.

claims.claim_pattern: Wearing a janeu or performing priestly purity rituals is required for Sikh liberation
aliases: Guru Nanak taught the sacred thread as the path to God
Caste purity rituals grant mukti in Sikhi
claims.explanation: Guru Nanak rejected the janeu as a mark of spiritual rank. Caste purity rites are not the Sikh path.
claims.correction: Sikh teaching rejects caste ritual-purity as the way to God.

claims.claim_pattern: Sikhi teaches that God can only be worshipped in one specific physical form
aliases: God in Sikhism must be worshipped as a particular idol or image
Sikh teaching confines Waheguru to one bodily form
Gurbani says God has only one physical form to worship
claims.explanation: Sikh teaching names God as Ik Onkar and Nirankar (the One, without form). Confining worship to one physical murti or bodily form contradicts Gurbani.
claims.correction: Sikhi does not teach that God can only be worshipped in one specific physical form. Devotion is to the formless One through Naam and the Guru Granth Sahib.
